title: Treatment of Private PSLE Candidates in Secondary School Posting Exercise
what_it_is: Treatment of Private PSLE Candidates in Secondary School Posting Exercise

sections.label: PSLE private candidates secondary placement
sections.summary: Private PSLE candidates are excluded from the Secondary One Posting Exercise but MOE facilitates their admission to secondary schools based on choices, results and vacancies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) in 2015, what is the number of Singaporean PSLE private candidates who have been posted to secondary schools not of their first choice even though they meet the cut-off point; (b) what is the Secondary One placement policy for such candidates; (c) what is the rationale to treat such candidates differently from those studying in mainstream schools during Secondary One placement exercises; and (d) whether the policy can be reviewed to uphold the principle of meritocracy.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: Hence, those who are not enrolled in our primary schools and are taking the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) as private candidates, are not included in this Secondary One Posting Exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: However, if such private candidates or students are interested and eligible to join mainstream secondary schools, the Ministry of Education (MOE) will facilitate their admission to a secondary school.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: MOE will take into account the students' choices of schools, PSLE results and available vacancies at the point of facilitation.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: As vacancies are limited, we may not always be able to offer these students a place in a school of their choice, but we will aim to match the students to a school appropriate to their academic learning needs.

sections.label: Facilitation requests for private candidates
sections.summary: Over the last five years, about 20 requests yearly were received from PSLE private candidates, and the majority were facilitated into a school of their choice.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: About the number, on average, over the last five years, we received about 20 requests each year from these PSLE private candidates to be facilitated into our mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: This is a very small number or percentage of the number of students who are not in our national primary schools.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And I would also like to inform the Member that we are able to facilitate the majority of these requests to one of the school choices of the students and some of them are also facilitated into their top choices.

sections.label: MOE facilitation and school vacancies
sections.summary: MOE will try its best to facilitate postings tagged to children's academic needs, considering available vacancies, and has facilitated the majority into schools of their choice.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Nevertheless, like what I said earlier, I assure the Member that MOE will try our best to facilitate, to ensure that the posting is tagged to the academic needs of the children and also we have to look at the vacancies available.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And I must say that from experience, we have been able to facilitate the majority of the students into the schools of their choice.
